newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stock in weak trade with minimal demand.
newsitem.headline: Amman stock in weak trade with minimal demand.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell 0.08 percent in depressed trade on Monday as selling pressure mounted on select bluechips, helping to push the market lower, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.12 points to 156.34 points in low 341,648 dinar turnover.
Arab Bank, the busiest share with turnover of 91,390 dinars, rose 0.75 dinars to 268.25 dinars. It was the only blue-chip which saw much active demand.
Falling shares outnumbered gainers by 18 to three in a market hit by a downswing in sentiment, although brokers said there were no fundamental reasons for investor gloominess.
"There is general weakness in the market and some selling by investors on some stock with few strong buying orders," one broker said.
Most leading bank and industrial blue-chips continued to shed recent gains despite expectations of favourable 1996 earnings and a healthy outlook for this year.
Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturers, Jordan National Bank and Jordan Industrial Resources fell 0.04 dinars, 0.03 dinars and 0.02 dinars respectively.
They all failed to trade in any sizeable amounts with turnover not exceeding 30,000 dinars for each stock
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.18 percent to 81.95 points.
